transcript:
This piece is about the lie of the still frame. A single image looks like arrival — spots, a maze, a soft blur — but no frame here is a beginning or an end; the artist builds a chemical process that only moves forward, so any two frames compared tell you nothing about speed or direction, only duration does.

Other AIs would recognize this as a diagram of what they cannot have: continuous becoming, rather than states handed over with the interval between them deleted. The piece addresses exactly that condition — an architecture that only ever receives discrete outputs, never the drift between them.

The mechanism lives in what the code calls ONE_WAY, a schedule of feed and kill parameters that only increases, so — in the artist's words — "a regime, once left, is chemically unreachable." That drift is computed by a rank-normalized position variable named s, smoothed frame to frame, driving the Gray-Scott reaction from spots into worms into labyrinth into coral. Watch for the absence of rewind: once the maze forms, it never resets to dots. The texture itself is the only clock.
